live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.what_this_node_is: An addition, made 2026-09-02, that answers QA finding F4 against THIS file: the staging tree /opt/blitzy-harness/cpg-input recorded in `archives[]` above is not immutable, and it no longer holds the bytes `archives[]` records. Nothing above this node was rewritten - `schema_version`, every existing key and every `archives[]` entry are exactly as they were measured on 2026-09-01 - because the retained measurement is the only record of what the tree once held and overwriting it would destroy the evidence of the drift. This node is the census of what the tree holds NOW, member by member, and the statement of what that costs the run's reproducibility.
live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.command:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, os, time
S = "/opt/blitzy-harness/cpg-input"
ROOTS = ("/opt/spark-src", "/opt/blitzy-harness")
started = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
inv = json.load(open("harness/artifacts/logs/cpg-input-inventory.json"))
ret = {a["staged_name"]: a for a in inv["archives"]}
peers = {}
for root in ROOTS:
    for dp, _dn, fns in os.walk(root):
        if os.path.abspath(dp) == S:
            continue
        for fn in fns:
            p = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            st = os.lstat(p)
            if os.path.isfile(p) and st.st_nlink > 1:
                peers.setdefault((st.st_dev, st.st_ino), []).append(p)
members = []
for n in sorted(os.listdir(S)):
    p = os.path.join(S, n)
    st = os.lstat(p)
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as fh:
        for c in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(c)
    d = h.hexdigest()
    r = ret.get(n, {"bytes": None, "sha256": None})
    members.append({
        "staged_name": n,
        "verdict": "MATCHES" if (r["bytes"], r["sha256"]) == (st.st_size, d) else "DRIFTED",
        "retained_bytes": r["bytes"], "live_bytes": st.st_size,
        "retained_sha256": r["sha256"], "live_sha256": d,
        "live_mtime_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(st.st_mtime)),
        "st_nlink": st.st_nlink,
        "hard_link_peers": sorted(peers.get((st.st_dev, st.st_ino), [])),
    })
mt = sorted(m["live_mtime_utc"] for m in members)
print(json.dumps({
    "census_started_utc": started,
    "census_finished_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    "staging_tree": S,
    "hard_link_peer_search_roots": list(ROOTS),
    "live_member_count": len(members),
    "retained_member_count": len(ret),
    "names_only_in_the_live_tree": sorted(set(m["staged_name"] for m in members) - set(ret)),
    "names_only_in_the_retained_inventory": sorted(set(ret) - set(m["staged_name"] for m in members)),
    "members_matching_the_retained_inventory": sum(1 for m in members if m["verdict"] == "MATCHES"),
    "members_drifted_from_the_retained_inventory": sum(1 for m in members if m["verdict"] == "DRIFTED"),
    "live_total_bytes": sum(m["live_bytes"] for m in members),
    "retained_total_bytes": sum(a["bytes"] for a in inv["archives"]),
    "live_minus_retained_bytes": sum(m["live_bytes"] for m in members) - sum(a["bytes"] for a in inv["archives"]),
    "members_with_st_nlink_gt_1": sum(1 for m in members if m["st_nlink"] > 1),
    "members_with_an_identified_hard_link_peer": sum(1 for m in members if m["hard_link_peers"]),
    "live_distinct_sha256": len(set(m["live_sha256"] for m in members)),
    "live_mtime_earliest_utc": mt[0], "live_mtime_latest_utc": mt[-1],
    "members": members,
}, indent=1))
PY

live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.census_method: Read-only. Nothing under /opt/blitzy-harness or /opt/spark-src was created, deleted, moved, relinked or re-staged. Per member: os.lstat for size, st_nlink and mtime, and sha256 over the whole file. A member is MATCHES only when BOTH its live size and its live sha256 equal the retained `archives[]` values for the same `staged_name`, and DRIFTED otherwise. A hard-link peer is identified by (st_dev, st_ino) identity - the same inode reached under another path - not by filename similarity, so a named peer is the same bytes by construction. The peer index walks /opt/spark-src and /opt/blitzy-harness for regular files with st_nlink > 1, excluding the staging directory itself.

The 39 matching members contribute nothing to the difference, so the whole of it is drift rather than a counting change.
live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.what_the_link_counts_mean: 32 of the 62 members are still hard links sharing an inode with a file in the shared build tree /opt/spark-src, so their bytes remain writable through that other path by anything that rebuilds that module. Every one of the 23 drifted members is in that set. The 30 members now at st_nlink == 1 are single-linked only because the build tree replaced the path that used to share their inode; all 30 still match, but they are frozen by accident rather than by design, and provisioning staged them the same way as the other 32.

hard_link_peers_by_name.reading: Every identified peer is under /opt/spark-src/**/target/. For 30 of the 32 the peer is now named original-<basename> - the name maven-shade-plugin gives the pre-shade artifact it displaces when it writes a shaded jar over the module's main artifact name. The staged member therefore no longer holds the shaded primary artifact it was staged as; it holds whatever content the inode now carries after a later `package` in the shared tree. This is the mechanism the measurements support, stated as an inference from the peer names and mtimes below rather than as an observation of the build itself, which this run did not perform and cannot inspect.

live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.one_to_one_assertion_status_on_the_live_: SUPERSEDED FOR THE LIVE TREE. The `one_to_one` key above - '62 archives, 62 distinct sha256 ... injective in both directions' - was true of the tree when it was measured on 2026-09-01 and is retained unchanged as that measurement. It is FALSE of the tree today: 62 names now carry only 45 distinct sha256 values, in 17 two-member groups. Every one of the 17 groups pairs a module's 'original-*' staged member with that same module's non-'original-' primary member, i.e. the primary's bytes are now identical to its own pre-shade sibling's. Injectivity, which AAP 0.5.1 requires of the input manifest, therefore cannot be re-established from this tree.

All 23 drifted members were last written between 2026-09-02T06:05:10Z and 06:25:38Z - three days after the graph was finished at 2026-08-30T19:18:42Z, and one day after `archives[]` above was measured. The drift is therefore entirely post-graph: for 23 of the 62 inputs, the bytes the graph was built from are no longer on disk anywhere this run can reach.

live_staging_tree_census_2026-09-02.reproducibility_limitation: THE SURVIVING STAGING TREE CANNOT RECREATE THE GRAPH AND CANNOT PROVE THE GRAPH'S INPUT BYTES. Its members are hard links into /opt/spark-src, a build tree shared with roughly 45 concurrent clones and writable by any of them, rather than immutable copies taken at staging time. 23 of the 62 members have since been rewritten through that other path, three days after the graph was written; 32 of the 62 are still linked and so can still change again. Re-running the frontend over this tree today would consume different bytes and produce a different graph, and no digest taken from this tree today attests to the graph /opt/blitzy-harness/cpg/spark.cpg (547,980,224 bytes, sha256 325887cf6c65377b1c5b9c127b1ea16807463313e82baf14cabb0e5c5aba3dc6). THAT IDENTITY WAS RE-ANCHORED ON 2026-09-03: when this census was taken the graph on disk was the 2026-09-01 generation, 541,309,809 bytes / sha256 4616845ab2b0de2b8e7d43598de0e18c2302be233149b933af3098b0aa4730c7, and this sentence named that SUPERSEDED pair; the re-provisioning of 2026-09-03T01:17:07Z replaced it, and the earlier graph is no longer on disk. The limitation itself is unchanged and if anything broader - a re-measurement on 2026-09-03 found all 62 members carrying st_nlink greater than 1, where this census found 32, so every member is now writable through another path (see byte_total_correction_2026-09-03, which also republishes the byte total this census compares against). The retained `archives[]` measurement above is the only surviving record of the staged bytes - for the three members whose figures were corrected to disk on 2026-09-03 that record is byte_total_correction_2026-09-03, which carries their 2026-09-01 bytes and digests verbatim, rather than `archives[]` - and it is a record rather than the bytes: the original content of the 23 drifted members is not recoverable, because the external build that overwrote it has exited and this run may not write, relink or re-stage anything under /opt/blitzy-harness/cpg-input or /opt/spark-src. This is a defect in how the input was staged, not a defect in the measurement, and it is recorded here rather than repaired because no repair is available from inside this run.
what_a_human_must_do: Stage the graph input as immutable, content-addressed COPIES - each file named by or stored under its own sha256, in a tree owned by the run and writable by nothing else - never as hard links or symlinks into a shared build tree. A hard link makes the staged bytes an alias of a mutable file, which is the whole of this defect.
Take the inventory AFTER the final build that produces the artifacts, from the copies rather than from the build tree, and make the frontend read the same copies the inventory measured.

Retain the verified input unchanged for as long as the graph is cited: mark the staging tree read-only, keep it out of any path a later build writes, and re-verify size and sha256 per member before every load, the way the graph's own identity is re-verified.

Where retention of the bytes is impossible, publish the graph together with its input manifest and treat the graph as unreproducible from that point on - state it, as this node does, rather than let a retained digest imply that the bytes it describes are still available.

byte_total_correction_2026-09-03.command:
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, os, time
S = "/opt/blitzy-harness/cpg-input"
start = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
names = sorted(os.listdir(S))
total = 0
digests = {}
nlink_gt1 = 0
per = {}
for n in names:
    p = os.path.join(S, n)
    st = os.lstat(p)
    total += st.st_size
    if st.st_nlink > 1:
        nlink_gt1 += 1
    h = hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
    digests.setdefault(h, []).append(n)
    per[n] = (st.st_size, h, st.st_nlink)
finish = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
inv = json.load(open("harness/artifacts/logs/cpg-input-inventory.json"))
arcs = inv["archives"]
# every figure below is printed from these measurements: member count, total bytes,
# distinct digests, st_nlink census, and the per-member comparison against archives[]
bad = [(a["staged_name"], a["bytes"], per[a["staged_name"]][0], a["sha256"],
        per[a["staged_name"]][1])
       for a in arcs if (a["bytes"], a["sha256"]) != per[a["staged_name"]][:2]]

byte_total_correction_2026-09-03.how_this_is_kept_from_recurring: harness/lib/verify_status_figures.py now asserts this file's arithmetic on every run, as a fourth family alongside its citation, self-consistency and command-equality families: `total_bytes` must equal the sum of its own `archives[]` byte figures, `archive_count` must equal the length of `archives[]`, and - when the shared staging tree is present - both must equal the measured sum and the member count on disk, with the disk half skipped with a stated reason rather than passed silently when the tree is absent. A four-byte drift in a self-consistent figure is exactly the class of defect that gate now fails on.
